title: Chrome zero-days: why that Relaunch button matters (CVE-2026-87491)
description:
Chrome keeps asking you to relaunch for a reason. Google has fixed at least seven Chrome zero-days in 2026 that attackers were already exploiting before a fix existed.

The latest reported, CVE-2026-87491, is an out-of-bounds write in V8, Chrome's JavaScript engine. According to the NVD description, a crafted web page could let a remote attacker run code inside Chrome's sandbox. Google said an exploit for it exists in the wild. A researcher reported it on August 6, 2026; the US agency CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 9 and gave federal agencies until September 12 to patch. It was fixed in Chrome 153.0.8010.36 and later.

Chrome downloads fixes in the background, but they only take effect after a relaunch. Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi are built on the same engine, so update them too.

Do this tonight: open the Chrome menu, then Help, then About Google Chrome. Let it update and click Relaunch. Then do the same in your other browsers.
